purpose: Remove both the unnecessary EQ4 hypothesis and the characteristic-zero restriction from the earlier common-basis matchgate barrier. This matters because the current bounded-occurrence carrier needs equality arity at most three only, and characteristic two was a plausible sign-cancellation escape route.

theorem.name: NO_COMMON_INVERTIBLE_BASIS_MAKES_EQ3_AND_OR3_BOTH_MATCHGATE_OVER_ANY_FIELD
theorem.statement: There is no invertible 2x2 basis S such that S^(tensor 3) EQ3 and (S^(-T))^(tensor 3) OR3 are both matchgate signatures. EQ4 is not required.
proof: Every matchgate signature obeys the combinatorial parity condition: support lies entirely on even or entirely on odd Hamming weights. This condition is field-independent.
Write S=[[a,c],[b,d]]. Invertibility plus parity of transformed EQ3 forces a,b,c,d nonzero, so put r=c/a and s=d/b; invertibility is r!=s.
If transformed EQ3 is even-parity, its odd layers give s^3=-1 and r^2 s=-1. Hence r^2=s^2.
If transformed EQ3 is odd-parity, its even layers give r^3=-1 and r s^2=-1. Hence again r^2=s^2.
In characteristic two, r^2=s^2 implies (r-s)^2=0, hence r=s in a field, contradicting invertibility. Thus EQ3 alone cannot be made parity-pure by an invertible basis in characteristic two.
Now assume characteristic is not two. From r^2=s^2 and r!=s we get s=-r.
Ignoring one common nonzero denominator, the transformed OR3 symmetric layers are g0=-3s^2+3s-1, g1=2rs-r+s^2-2s+1, g2=-r^2-2rs+2r+s-1, g3=3r^2-3r+1.
Substitute s=-r. Then g1=-r^2+r+1 and g3=3r^2-3r+1, so g3+3g1=4. Therefore OR3 cannot be even-parity (which would require g1=g3=0).
Also g0=-3r^2-3r-1 and g2=r^2+r-1, so g0+3g2=-4. Therefore OR3 cannot be odd-parity (which would require g0=g2=0).

In every field of characteristic not two, 4 is nonzero. Hence OR3 violates matchgate parity in every invertible basis that makes EQ3 parity-pure. Combined with the characteristic-two case, no field admits such a common basis.

killed: One common 2x2 holographic basis converting the bounded-occurrence EQ3 variable layer and OR3 clause layer simultaneously into ordinary matchgate signatures over characteristic zero
